newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka might tax cigarettes to boost health services.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka might tax cigarettes to boost health services.

text.p: Sri Lanka could levy additional tax on alcohol and tobacco to raise funds to improve its health services, government officials said on Thursday.
They said a task force on the health sector has recommended that each cigarette be taxed an additional two cents and every bottle of alcohol 50 cents.
Cigarettes currently are subject to an average excise duty of more than 70 percent while beer attracts 15 percent and liquor 56 percent.
The study did not say how much money the government aimed to raise from additional taxes, but added that some of it would be spent to promote the use of contraceptives.

Health Minister A.H.M. Fowzie was quoted by the state-owned Daily News as saying on Thursday that the recommendations would be presented to President Chandrika Kumaratunga later this month. ($1 = 58 rupees)
